psf_cap_vs_market_gap.binding_constraint: The absolute $2.2M ceiling, NOT PSF. Most in-area freehold 3BR already trade WITHIN the ~$1,650-1,910 psf band; they blow the budget because they are 1,200-1,400 sqft, pushing total price to $2.3-2.5M.
psf_cap_vs_market_gap.takeaway: The cheapest route into the band is a smaller 3BR (1,050-1,250 sqft) at mid-$1,600s-$1,900s psf, OR a low-PSF project (Fiorenza ~$1,450, Jade ~$1,700, Waterline/Palm Grove ~$1,620). Chasing larger 1,300+ sqft units forces you over $2.2M even at reasonable PSF.

filter_tradeoffs.units_vs_psf_vs_region: The intersection {freehold/999-yr + post-2000 + >=1,000 sqft 3BR + <=$2.2M} is tight and splits cleanly: (1) SIZE OF DEVELOPMENT (세대수) vs TENURE — the large developments (393-1,052 units) that carry 'hidden' low-PSF 3BR stacks (Kovan Regency, Kovan Residences, Affinity, Riversails, Garden Residences, Stars of Kovan, Bartley Ridge) are almost all 99-YEAR leasehold in this geography. The freehold stock that clears is boutique/mid (The Quinn 139u, The Waterline 103u, Palm Grove 111u, Fiorenza 28u) — so you trade inventory/optionality for tenure. Flamingo Valley (393u, FH) is the rare large freehold exception, and even it only clears at the $2.2M ceiling. (2) REGION vs PRICE — D19 Hougang/Bartley freehold mid-size delivers the cleanest fits at the LOWEST psf ($1,616-1,940); D15 freehold costs ~$300-400k more for an equivalent 3BR and clears only at the ceiling (Flamingo) or just over it (Carpmael, Elliot, One Amber); strict D14 Eunos/Paya Lebar has effectively nothing freehold >=1,000 sqft in band (Paya Lebar Residences overpriced, Urban Treasures 3BR too small). (3) NEW IMPLICATION — you generally cannot get all three of {freehold, large-development hidden-stack optionality, <=$2.2M} at once here. Keep freehold + budget and you accept a small development; want a big-development hidden stack and you must flex to 99-yr. The single best resolution this week is The Quinn (freehold, mid-size, D19 Bartley, $1,940 psf, ~$124k budget headroom).
